title: AW27 Men's Couture Craft and Techniques
summary: Craft for AW27 menswear: natural dyeing, double-faced finishing, intricate weaving and patinated leather.
research_period: Pitti Filati, June 2026; Première Vision, Lineapelle and Milano Unica, September 2026; forecaster reports to November 2026

sections.heading: How this forecast was built
sections.body: Pre-runway forecast. The AW27 shows run from January to March 2027. This report is built from the 2026 yarn, fabric and leather fairs (Pitti Filati in June; Première Vision, Lineapelle and Milano Unica in September), published forecaster views and the SS27 runways. Forecut will update it after the shows.

sections.heading: The evidence
sections.body:
- Van den Hoek describes natural dyes from tea, coffee, corn and tree bark, whose limits give richer colour gradations<sup>[1]</sup>
- Separable double-faced woollens return in more varied weights; ultrafine yarns and tight knits make wool lighter and softer, with thermal comfort without synthetics<sup>[2]</sup>
- APLF's AW27 leather directions run from raw, vegetable-tanned and waxed pull-up leathers to ultra-supple nappas and cashmere-hand suedes, glazed and moiré luxury leathers, and rubbery, holographic and laser-engraved experimental leathers<sup>[3]</sup>

sections.heading: Translating
sections.body:
- Naturally dyed knits.
- Double-faced coats.
- Patinated leather.
